policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV text reads simply 'Father'; the expansion 'Our Father, who art in heaven' stands only in the mapped textual note as a margin reading, so the text renders the short address.
ASV ends the petitions at 'Thy kingdom come.' with no rendering of 'Thy will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.'
ASV text ends 'And bring us not into temptation.'; 'but deliver us from the evil one' appears only in the mapped textual note as a margin addition.
ASV 'a friend of mine' renders the possessive mou; the omitting reading would give only 'a friend'.
Word order only: both philon autou and autou philon yield ASV 'because he is his friend'.

ASV 'as many as he needeth' is plural, rendering the plural genitive hoson (r00); the singular hoson of r01 would give 'as much as'. The 'Or, whatsoever things' note is an alternative rendering and does not decide.
ASV 'of which of you' renders a partitive genitive equally well with or without ex; the preposition leaves no separate mark in the English.

ASV text carries the loaf-and-stone clause ('shall his son ask a loaf, and he give him a stone? or'), which the mapped textual note reports some authorities omit; the text therefore has the longer reading.

ASV supplies 'and he give' in the parallel first clause where no kai stands in Greek, so the second 'and he for a fish give him a serpent' is English parallelism and does not show kai against interrogative me, which ASV leaves untranslated in a question.
Word order only: both give ASV 'give him a serpent'.
ASV renders an explicit conditional, 'Or if he shall ask an egg', where the parallel v.11 without ean has no 'if' ('shall his son ask a loaf'); the 'if' answers ean aitese.
ASV's 'will he give him a scorpion?' is a question either way; the interrogative particle me is not separately rendered.
ASV 'casting out a demon that was dumb' attaches kophon attributively to the noun; the longer reading's 'and it was dumb' would give a coordinate clause, which the ASV does not have.
Presence or absence of the article before the appositive leaves no mark in ASV 'By Beelzebub the prince of the demons'; the notes are an alternative rendering and a Greek gloss.
Word order only: both yield ASV 'sought of him a sign from heaven'.
All three are orderings of autoi hymon kritai; each yields ASV 'therefore shall they be your judges'.
ASV 'But if I by the finger of God cast out demons' states the subject as English requires with the first-person verb; the emphatic ego leaves no distinct mark.
ASV 'when a stronger than he shall come upon him' is indefinite, matching the anarthrous comparative; the article of r01 would give 'the stronger'.
ASV 'a stronger than he' renders the genitive of comparison autou, which the omitting reading lacks.
ASV 'and finding none, he saith' has no 'then'; the added tote is unrendered.
ASV 'he findeth it swept and garnished' names two participles only; scholazonta ('empty') is not rendered.
The candidates differ only in the placement of hepta; ASV 'seven other spirits more evil than himself' fits any of them.
ASV 'they enter in' renders the compound eiselthonta; the simplex elthonta would give 'they come'.
Word order only: both yield ASV 'a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice'.
Menoun and menounge alike are rendered 'Yea rather'; the enclitic ge leaves no mark.
ASV 'and keep it' supplies the object English transitive 'keep' requires; the pronoun does not show whether auton stood in the Greek.
ASV repeats the noun, 'This generation is an evil generation'; the omitting reading would give only 'This generation is evil'.
ASV 'seeketh after a sign' renders zetei and the compound epizetei alike; the prefix leaves no distinct mark.
ASV reads 'the sign of Jonah' twice with no 'the prophet'.
The article with the proper name is not rendered in English; ASV has 'Jonah' either way.
Word order only: both yield ASV 'became a sign unto the Ninevites'.
ASV 'The men of Nineveh' renders the gentilic andres Nineuitai and the place name Nineui alike; the English idiom does not distinguish them.
ASV opens the sentence asyndetically, 'No man, when he hath lighted a lamp'; the connective de of r01 is unrendered.
Phengos and phos are both rendered 'the light'; the ASV wording does not distinguish them.
ASV supplies possessives freely in this verse ('thy body' answers an anarthrous-possessive-less tou somatos), so 'thine eye' does not show whether sou stood in the Greek.
ASV reads 'when thine eye is single' with no inferential 'therefore'; the added oun is unrendered.
Word order only: both yield ASV 'having no part dark'.
ASV 'a Pharisee asketh him' is present tense, rendering erota; the imperfect erota of r01 would give 'was asking'/'besought'.
ASV reads 'a Pharisee', not 'a certain Pharisee'; ASV renders tis with 'a certain' in this chapter (11:27, 'a certain woman'), so the added tis is absent.
ASV has the adversative 'but these ought ye to have done'; without de the clause would stand asyndetic.
ASV 'not to leave the other undone' renders pareinai and aphienai alike; the English phrase does not distinguish them.
ASV reads only 'Woe unto you!' with no 'scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites'.
ASV 'the men that walk over them' uses a relative clause; the attributive article is not separately rendered, and 'the men' stands either way.
ASV 'ye are witnesses' renders the noun-plus-copula martyres este; the finite martyreite would give 'ye bear witness'.
ASV states an object, 'ye build their tombs', which the base leaves the verb without; the words are not marked as an ASV supply.
ASV 'persecute' renders dioxousin and the compound ekdioxousin alike.
English requires 'the blood of Abel' whether or not the Greek article stands; the ASV wording does not decide.
English requires 'the blood of Zachariah' whether or not the Greek article stands; the ASV wording does not decide.
ASV 'And when he was come out from thence' renders kakeithen exelthontos autou; r01's 'And as he said these things unto them' is a different clause the ASV does not have.
ASV 'laying wait for him, to catch something out of his mouth' has no rendering of zetountes ('seeking').
ASV ends the verse at 'out of his mouth' with no 'that they might accuse him'.
